answer.generated: The parallel processing capability of artificial neural networks allows them to distribute computational tasks across multiple nodes, which enhances their robustness against missing data during training. This distributed processing means that if some parts of the network fail or lose data, the overall system can still function effectively, as it relies on the collective input from all nodes. Consequently, this architecture enables ANNs to produce meaningful outputs even when trained on incomplete datasets, making them particularly suitable for scenarios where data integrity cannot be guaranteed.
